pr_title: distribution: retry downloading schema config on retryable error
pr_body:
fixes #43267

**- What I did**
Add a simple retry mechanism to the schema download with exponential back-off, max retries, and that respects context cancellation.

**- How to verify it**
I think the tests cover it pretty well?

**- Description for the changelog**
Add retries for schema manifest downloads.

**- A picture of a cute animal (not mandatory but encouraged)**
![cat-typing](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/152569/155523672-94ba7096-7835-4b92-9a21-bac90f73b52c.gif)

issue_context.title: Retry required for manifest config blobs
issue_context.body:
**Describe the results you received:**
The manifest config blob of docker schema 2 manifest is directly pulled in [distribution/pull_v2.go](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/v20.10.12/distribution/pull_v2.go#L654-L663) without any retry logic while layer blobs are pulled via `DownloadManager` with a [retry logic](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/v20.10.12/distribution/xfer/download.go#L296-L304) (max 5 times).

**Describe the results you expected:**

The manifest config blob is retried on network failure as layers are retried by the `DownloadManager`.

**Moby version:**

`v20.10.12`
comments:
Not sure exactly why no retry was implemented for the manifest itself, although I think the main reason for the download-manager was to control the number of parallel layer downloads (which could more easily cause network congestion); handling of manifest vs layers also is quite different there, so I guess it won't be easy to add it to the existing download-managers (so not sure if it would make sense to try to shoe-horn it into that).

A retry could possibly make sense though

review_comments:
I haven't checked out the branch locally yet to compare, but glancing over the tests, it looks like there's quite some common boilerplating code. Perhaps it's possible to combine (some of) the tests and use a sub-tests.

Just some quick examples that use sub-tests; 

https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/7b9275c0da707b030e62c96b679a976f31f929d3/daemon/volumes_linux_test.go#L10

https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/9e8cf1016ead200aea31d7ff381ba2ed01416ddb/builder/dockerfile/evaluator_test.go#L27

ticker will still run after this and never will stop. 
Better use a `time. NewTimer` as a `Timer` will present a single event.

Ah, that would be me to blame. I always confuse them (but noticed that the `xfer` was using a ticker, and I recalled some oddities when to do / don't use them https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/43291#discussion_r813871236
Ah, I guess there it's using it for the retrying in XX seconds loop, so it's slightly different; in this case it would probably need to take the whole loop here 🤔
I did a quick search for the issue I remembered; and I think that issue was when using `time.After()` see https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/38522
I've changed it back to `time.NewTimer()`. I think using time.After() makes a leak if the other select succeeds (in the case the context times out).
